text:
Amir (Eng): I booked a non-refundable fare for a client trip but had to move my flight due to a meeting shift. Airline charged $215 change fee on my personal card. They later emailed a "fee waiver" code and applied it as a credit to my account; however my card still shows the $215 charge. Can we get reimbursed or do we need to wait for the refund to hit my card?

Tess (Finance): Short: we reimburse only actual expenses after bank charge is final. If the airline posts a refund/credit back to your card, submit that proof and we won't reimburse. If the charge remains and airline issued a ticket credit (not refunded), we can advance reimbursement if you have written manager approval AND you attach the airline waiver email showing the credit and timeline. We'll then reconcile once the refund posts.

Amir (Eng): The waiver email says "account credit" and includes a reference number but doesn't explicitly say "refunded to card." The agent told me it would be a future credit toward a new ticket.

Nadia (People Ops): Policy nuance: we avoid duplicative payments. If airline only issued future credit, that's not a refund; we can reimburse the out-of-pocket cost if manager approves AND you commit to applying the airline credit on the next company booking or return the credit value to the company if used for personal travel. Attach waiver + agent transcript.

Tess (Finance): Docs we need: 1) airline waiver email or agent chat screenshot with reference number, 2) card statement showing the charge, 3) manager approval (Concur comment or email) if you're asking for an advance reimbursement, and 4) a short attestation from you about whether you'll apply the credit to future company travel or return it.

Amir (Eng): If I ask Finance to wait for refund, any timeline guidance?

Tess (Finance): Typical refund timelines vary (7-60 days). If it's under 30 days we're usually OK waiting. If you need cashflow earlier and manager approves, Finance can process an interim reimbursement flagged as "advance - pending refund" and we'll reconcile when the airline processes the refund.

travel-bot: Policy note: "Change fees and force-majeure waivers: reimbursements are made for actual out-of-pocket expenses. Interim advances are allowed with manager sign-off and clear documentation; returned airline credits must be applied to future company travel or refunded to the company." Internal travel policy: https://redwoodinference.com/policies/travel#airfare :link:

Nadia (People Ops): Threshold reminder: manager approval is sufficient for advances <= $300. Advances > $300 need People Ops sign-off. Reimbursements funded after final refund clearance don't need advance approval.

Amir (Eng): Got it. I'll upload the waiver email + card statement and ask my manager for a note. Thanks!

Tess (Finance): One more coding note: when you submit, set expense code to "Travel > Air - change fee / advance" and include the airline reference number in the expense description for reconciliation.

Amir (Eng): Will do. Closing after upload. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
